reserveReview.rationale: Classification-only extension researched 2026-10-20: the exact nOPAL positions endpoint binds pending withdrawal request 15 to OALS2T on Plume, token 0x04e5a6f7ee9977d38f57945c31b72178c9cf1c06, in yieldAssets slug liquid-stone. Its disclosed value is 650202.1325963091; no current allocation percentage is authored. The pending-withdrawals metadata row is private-credit redemption receivable exposure to the same LiquidStone II obligor, not immediately liquid stablecoins. Admission relies on the companion producer guard requiring yield/liquid-stone/OALS2T; a different underlying must fail closed pending a new review. Its zero percentage is a live-key classification placeholder like the existing USDG row, not an observation of zero current exposure. The October 9 USDG classification and all other historic classifications retain their original evidence; every pre-existing percentage and compositionAsOf remains the September 4 snapshot. This review establishes neither current whole-book composition nor new custody safeguards. BlackOpal/Nest do not disclose a whole-OALS2T contractual maturity maximum or stressed realization horizon. nTBILL's qualified up-to-four-day redemption estimate likewise does not establish a receipt maturity maximum or unconditional stressed settlement bound.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Classification metadata for exact live-adapter source keys; historical percentages remain the Nest positions/NAV snapshot fetched 2026-09-04, not current whole-book composition.
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: OALS2T's obligor-level receivable composition, fund service providers, and any fund-level financial audit are not public. Stablecoin and nTBILL legs are identified.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Nest documents that underlying-asset cash and securities sit with third-party custodians rather than Nest itself, and BlackOpal describes LiquidStone II as a single-investor sub-fund of a Brazilian FIDC holding receivables acquired via true sale, which supports segregated, bankruptcy-remote treatment. The FIDC's custodian, administrator, and obligor-level positions are not named publicly, no fund-level financial attestation exists, and rehypothecation terms are not published.
